pages.text: Primary operator page checked: JR East uses preliminary earthquake tremors to provide Shinkansen warning information, which can also inform conventional train emergency stops. Evidence anchors: detects preliminary earthquake tremors (P waves). immediately issues earthquake warning information.

Primary operator investigation page checked: earthquake detection can cause overhead-line power interruption; equipment onboard detects the interruption and initiates an emergency stop. Evidence anchors: the emergency brake is applied. the power cut is detected onboard.

Independent USGS specialist page checked: early warning begins after rupture, rather than forecasting an earthquake. P waves arrive first. Stronger S/surface shaking can arrive later. Signals can arrive ahead of that shaking and initiate protective action. Evidence anchors: not earthquake prediction. already started. fastest-moving seismic waves. slower moving, and generally more damaging. many times faster than seismic waves. slowing a train.

JMA warning-limits page checked: usable warning time can be very short, especially close to the earthquake. Magnitude/intensity estimates also have limits. Evidence anchor: the warning may not be transmitted before strong tremors hit.

Current JR East earthquake initiatives page checked: the operator describes ongoing improvements to seismometers, external information inputs and power-interruption response. No precise warning seconds are claimed in this video. Evidence anchor: Measures for Emergency Stopping of Trains.
